claim: Moulin Castelas in Les Baux offers free mill visits and tastings year-round with no reservation, weekdays 8:30am-6:30pm and weekends 10am-1pm / 2:30pm-6:30pm.
quote: Visit of the mill and olive oil tastings are free and available all year round. Neither tours nor tastings require a reservation – just come on by!

claim: Moulin Jean-Marie Cornille is the historic cooperative oil mill in Maussane-les-Alpilles producing AOP Vallée des Baux-de-Provence olive oil.
quote: Moulin Cornille - Huile d'olives AOP de la Vallée des Baux de Provence

claim: At Moulin Cornille self-guided tours run Mon–Fri 9:30-11:45 and 13:30-16:30 for €4; guided tours by appointment at €6.50; shop open Mon-Fri 9:30-12:30 and 13:30-18:00, Sat until 18:00.
quote: Self-guided tours from Monday to Friday from 9.30am – 11.45am and 1:30 p.m. – 4:30 p.m. for €4 (free for children under 10... Guided tours by appointment Monday to Friday at 10:30 a.m. or 2:00 p.m. for €6.50

claim: The AOP Vallée des Baux-de-Provence blends at least two of four olive varieties — Salonenque (sweet, creamy), Aglandau (spicy), Grossane (grapefruit aromas), Verdale (herbaceous, green apple) — with Picholine as a complement, and counts 16 mills in the appellation area.
quote: Salonenque... gives the oil a sweet, fruity and creamy character... Aglandau... gives the oil its ardency... Grossane... grapefruit aromas... Verdale... herbaceous and green apple aromas... 16 in the appellation area.

claim: Moulin du Calanquet near Saint-Rémy, a family mill founded in 2000 by Anne and Gilles Brun, offers guided tours through olive grove and mill plus tastings of monovarietal oils, tapenades and jams, in French or English.
quote: At the end of the tour, visitors enjoy a tasting of various olive oils produced at the mill, and can sample tapenades, jams, and olives from tasting stations.

claim: From the 2023 vintage, AOP Les Baux-de-Provence became the first French wine appellation to require 100% organic viticulture across all producers.
quote: From the 2023 vintage, the AOP Les Baux-de-Provence will be the first 100% organic wine appellation.

claim: Château Romanin near Saint-Rémy offers a 1-hour guided tour with tasting at €20/person and a 2-hour prestige version at €80, showcasing biodynamic vines and its 'Cathedral Cellar' carved into the Alpilles rock by architect Serge Hennemann in 1992.
quote: A 1-hour guided tour and tasting costs €20 per person, while a 2-hour prestige tour with tasting is €80 per person.

claim: Mas de la Dame, at the foot of Les Baux, is run by Caroline Missoffe and Anne Poniatowski over 58 ha of vines and 28 ha of olives — certified organic since 1999 and now biodynamic — with tastings by reservation of wines, olive oil and tapenade.
quote: Mas de la Dame... 58 hectares of vines and 28 hectares of olive trees... private wine tastings are organized upon reservation

claim: Domaine Hauvette in Saint-Rémy, founded 1988 by Dominique Hauvette (named Vigneronne de l'année 2020 by Revue du Vin de France), farms ~17 ha biodynamically since 2003 with vinification in concrete eggs without sulfur.
quote: Today, she cultivates approximately 17 hectares, primarily in biodynamic farming since 2003... aging is done systematically in concrete eggs which accentuate the minerality

claim: Domaine de Trévallon was declassified to Vin de Pays (now IGP Alpilles) in 1993 when the new AOC Les Baux capped Cabernet Sauvignon at 20%, because Eloi Dürrbach's signature blend is 50/50 Cabernet Sauvignon / Syrah.
quote: At the time of the creation of AOC Baux de Provence in 1993, the Vineyard was degraded to Vin de Pays: too many Cabernet Sauvignon, limited to 20% of the blend in the new appellation!

claim: Mas de Gourgonnier near Mouriès, run by the Cartier family with 38 ha of vines and 18 ha of olives, was one of France's first certified organic wineries in the 1970s.
quote: Mas de Gourgonnier, with 38 hectares of grapevines and 18 hectares of olive groves... In the 1970s, this family estate was one of the first officially certified organic wineries.

claim: Mouriès' weekly Provençal market is held Wednesday mornings 8am-12:30pm on Cours Paul Révoil (temporarily relocated to Parc du Moulin Peyre from 1 October 2025 until end of March 2026 for roadworks).
quote: Due to construction work on Cours Paul Révoil, the weekly market will be temporarily relocated to Parc du Moulin Peyre from Wednesday, 1 October 2025 until the end of March 2026.

claim: The Maussane-les-Alpilles Provençal market takes place every Thursday morning 8am-1pm on Place Henri Giraud, featuring tapenade, cracked olives, goat cheeses and crafts.
quote: The Maussane-les-Alpilles market takes place on Place Henri Giraud every Thursday from 8am to 1pm.

claim: The Saint-Rémy-de-Provence market is held every Wednesday year-round 8am-1pm across Place de la République, Boulevard Marceau, Boulevard Gambetta and surrounding streets, with a free shuttle from the Petite Crau car park every 15 min.
quote: The market is held all year round on Wednesday between 8 am and 1 pm... free shuttle bus service from the Petite Crau car park between 9am and 1pm, running every 15 minutes.

claim: Maillane holds a Thursday morning market on avenue Auguste Daillan (Place de l'Église) from ~8am to 12:30pm.
quote: Le marché de Maillane se tient régulièrement le jeudi... à partir de 8 h... les vendeurs commencent à plier bagage à partir de 12 h 30.

claim: Eyguières has two weekly markets — Tuesday morning (Rue des Frères Perret / Place Monier, ~20 stalls, 8am-1pm) and Saturday morning (Place Thiers, ~25 selected vendors, 8am-12:30pm).
quote: le marché du mardi offre une grande variété de produits... le samedi met à l'honneur des vendeurs sélectionnés pour la qualité de leurs produits
